item.name: Batch Examples

request.description: This is the filtered batch call used to gather the data from a ECY2 device in the ECY Hub backend. It contains multiple examples of using layered filters. The ECY Hub only cares about specific data so its not necessary to include all of the data from each endpoint.

item.description:
# Batch operation

Allows to combine multiple requests.

The batch api is an independant endpoint, i.e. no special  
code is needed in servlets or endpoints to be compatible with the batch  
api.

URL: {base}/batch

The requests are executed in the order they are defined in the request body.

Request fields:

- _id_ (optional): String to uniquely tag  
    sub-requests. The response body will contain the associated id of each  
    request making it easier to parse the response.
    
- _method_ (optional): String specifying the HTTP method, default value is GET.
    
- _url_: Path of the request. Query Parameters are supported.
    
- _headers_ (optional): Headers of the request.
    
- _body_ (optional): Body of the request.
    

Response fields:

- _id_: String specified in the request if any.
    
- _url_: Only displayed if no id specified.
    
- _status_: HTTP code of the response.
    
- _headers_: Headers of the response if any.
    
- _body_: Body of the response if any.

item.name: Site Element Examples
item.description: This folder contains example calls to create a building, floor, space, & equipment for each. It also contains the calls to assign a dashboard to each, link devices, and link points from a connector. These examples are not meant to be used generally, but as an exercise or demonstration. Each project site likely has its own unique attributes - these will help guide you.

item.name: Query Parameters
item.description:
# Query parameters description | Name | Description | Example | | --- | --- | --- | | $select | Limit the values returned. Values can be separated by commas to
select multiple fields or multiple $select parameter can be set in the
query string.

Support wildcard character.
Support nested parameters, parentheses are used to specify nested parameters.
Combination of wildcard and nested parameters is supported. | _GET {services}/{service-name}?$select=,_

_GET {services}/{service-name}?$select=&$select=_

_GET {services}/{service-name}?$select=\*_

_GET {services}/{service-name}?$select=($select=)_

_GET {services}/{service-name}?$select=\*($select=\*)_ | | levels | Limits the number of recursion of data in element hierarchy returned in the payload.

0 means no data is written, useful when other kind of data is written, metadata for example. | _GET {services}/{service-name}?levels=0_

_GET {services}/{service-name}?levels=2_ | | metadata | If specified, the results will return metadata related to the schema of the values.

Possible values:
1\. A positive number: Indicates the number of recursion of metadata in element hierarchy returned in the payload.
2.
'all': Returns metadata of all elements hierarchy, no limit of
recursion. This is the default value when an invalid or no value is
specified. | _GET {services}/{service-name}?metadata=1_

_GET {services}/{service-name}?metadata=3_

_GET {services}/{service-name}?metadata=all_

_GET {services}/{service-name}?metadata_ |
